item.title: New accessibility updates for Microsoft Certification exams
item.description:
Preparing for a Microsoft Certification exam? Explore upcoming case study updates and new options for scheduling approved accommodations online.

 

If you're preparing for a Microsoft Certification exam, two upcoming changes may make your exam experience easier to navigate and schedule. The case study interface is being redesigned for greater readability and accessibility, and Pearson's accommodations process is becoming more streamlined. 

Certification exams should give every candidate a clear opportunity to demonstrate what they know. By making complex case studies easier to navigate and reducing friction in the accommodations process, these updates are designed to help candidates focus more fully on the skills being assessed.

Here's what is changing, when the updates will be available, and what you need to know before scheduling your exam.

A redesigned case study experience

Case study questions ask you to work through a detailed business scenario while answering related questions. Because that can mean viewing a large amount of information at once, the experience has been redesigned with readability, accessibility, and navigation in mind.

The updated case study format has begun rolling out, with the goal of making it available for all exams and languages by the end of the calendar year. The exam sandbox is expected to fully reflect the new format by the end of October 2026.

New features include:

1. A cleaner full-screen layout. View the question and supporting scenario side by side, then use the splitter bar to adjust how much space each receives.

New full-screen case study layout

 

2. A responsive layout. On smaller displays or when using zoom, magnification, or other assistive setups, the interface shifts to a single-column reading order. The question, answer area, and scenario content appear vertically, reducing the need for horizontal scrolling.

Responsive single-column layout

item.title: AI-powered + human-focused: Powering workforce transformation
item.description:
How Microsoft combines the reach and personalization of AI with human expertise to turn workforce learning into business impact.

When we think about AI transformation, we have to start with employees. There is simply no way around it. You can deploy the technology and set ambitious goals, but if people do not have the confidence, skills, and support to use AI in their work, transformation will not happen. Employees are the ones who turn AI from an experiment into real business impact.

Microsoft’s skilling approach brings together two complementary ideas: AI-powered skilling and human-focused learning. AI-powered experiences extend reach, personalization, and access. Human-focused experiences provide context, trust, dialogue, and connection.

The point is not to choose between AI and people. It’s to combine their strengths in a portfolio that can meet different workforce needs, organizational goals, levels of readiness, and learning preferences.

item.title: Updates to Azure Cosmos DB and Power Platform Developer Certifications
item.description:
What's changing for Azure Cosmos DB and Power Platform Developer Certifications? 

Developers aren't building the same applications they were just a few years ago.

Today, they're creating cloud-native solutions, integrating AI experiences, connecting data across platforms, and working with tools that evolve at an unprecedented pace. As developer roles continue to expand, the skills they need and the certifications that validate those skills must evolve too.

We're making updates to Microsoft Certifications for Azure Cosmos DB and Microsoft Power Platform developers. These changes help ensure that certifications continue to reflect the real-world skills developers use every day while helping learners demonstrate expertise in today's rapidly changing technology landscape.

Azure Cosmos DB Developer Certification evolves with modern development 

When Exam DP-420 was first introduced, it focused on validating the skills needed to build applications with Azure Cosmos DB.

Since then, the role of an Azure Cosmos DB developer has expanded significantly. Developers are now building cloud-native applications, designing modern application architectures, and increasingly creating AI-powered experiences that rely on data stored in Azure Cosmos DB.

To better reflect this broader role, we're updating the certification's name and level. The updated certification will be Microsoft Certified: Azure Cosmos DB AI Developer Associate. If you hold this certification, the name change will appear automatically; no action is required.

The updated certification will continue to validate the core Azure Cosmos DB development skills learners rely on today, while placing greater emphasis on modern application development patterns and AI-related scenarios that developers increasingly encounter in their work.

What does this mean for current certification holders? 

If you've already earned the certification, your achievement remains valid.

When the update takes effect, the certification name and level will automatically be updated on your transcript. You'll continue to renew your certification through the existing renewal process, and no additional action is required to maintain your credential.

Key dates

  • Certification name update effective: October 6, 2026
  • Updated exam available: October 6, 2026

Exam PL-400 Is Becoming AB-400 

We're also updating Exam PL-400 to AB-400: Extending Microsoft Power Platform Solutions with Code and AI, effective October 16, 2026.

This change reflects the way Power Platform developers are building solutions today. Modern development increasingly includes AI integrations, custom code experiences, intelligent agents, and advanced extensibility capabilities across the Microsoft ecosystem.

The refreshed AB-400 exam will continue to validate the core skills expected of Power Platform developers while incorporating newer capabilities and development patterns, including:

  • Power Apps code apps
  • Microsoft Foundry agent integration
  • Copilot Studio agent integration
  • AI-powered application development scenarios
  • Modern extensibility and customization approaches

What's staying the same? 

While the exam number is changing, the certification earned remains unchanged.

Learners who pass the exam will continue to earn the Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Developer Associate certification. The value of the credential, recognition from employers, and renewal process all remain the same.

The transition from PL-400 to AB-400 simply helps align the exam within Microsoft's certification portfolio while ensuring that the skills measured reflect the latest Power Platform capabilities.

Important transition dates

  • The updated AB-400 exam will be available beginning October 16, 2026, and registration is available today. Register now
  • October 16, 2026: Registration for PL-400 closes, and registration opens exclusively for AB-400.
  • Learners who register for PL-400 on or before October 16 can continue to schedule and take the exam through October 30, 2026.

What This Means for Learners 

Technology continues to evolve, and certifications should evolve with it.

These updates help ensure Microsoft Certifications remain aligned to the skills developers are using in modern application development, AI integration, and cloud-native architectures. Whether you're building AI-enabled applications with Azure Cosmos DB or extending Microsoft Power Platform solutions with code and AI, your certifications will continue to represent relevant, in-demand expertise.

As you plan your next learning milestone, explore AI Skills Navigator to discover certifications and training opportunities aligned to your goals.

item.title: New Microsoft 365 Certified: AI Services Administrator Associate Certification

item.title: New exam for Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Administrator Associate Certification
item.description:
The new Windows Server Certification exam is here. One exam, in-demand hybrid skills—and a limited-time beta discount. Secure your spot before it fills up.

Today’s IT infrastructure is more distributed than ever, spanning on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments and increasingly exposed to cyberthreats. Organizations need administrators who can secure, manage, and operate across this complexity to protect their valuable infrastructure.

To support this shift, we’re evolving the Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Certification and renaming it the Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Administrator Associate Certification. This updated Microsoft Certification validates your knowledge of deploying, implementing, managing, securing, and troubleshooting Windows Server. As part of this change, we’ve consolidated two exams to one. Effective September 2026, to earn this Certification, you’ll need to pass Exam AZ-802: Administering Windows Server, currently in beta.

Is this the right Certification for you?

The Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Administrator Associate Certification focuses on the practical skills needed to manage and secure Windows Server across Azure and on-premises environments, validating the ability to:

  • Deploy and manage Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS).
  • Manage Windows Server instances and workloads in a hybrid environment.
  • Manage virtual machines (VMs).
  • Implement and manage an on-premises and hybrid networking infrastructure.
  • Manage storage and file services.
  • Secure Windows Server infrastructure.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot Windows Server environments.

Candidates for this Certification administer identity, security, management, compute, networking, storage, and monitoring for Windows Server, and collaborate closely with architects, administrators, and engineers. 

They should have experience administering Windows Server by using technologies such as Windows Admin Center, Hyper-V, PowerShell, Azure Arc, Azure Monitor, Azure Update Manager, and Microsoft Defender for Cloud. They should also be familiar with AD DS.

What’s new in Exam AZ-802

Exam AZ-802 replaces:

  • Exam AZ-800: Administering Windows Server Hybrid Core Infrastructure
  • Exam AZ-801: Configuring Windows Server Hybrid Advanced Services

Both exams will be retired in September 2026.

The new exam provides a focused, streamlined validation by combining essential skills into one experience while prioritizing the most relevant scenarios for modern administrators.

Key updates include:

  • A unified exam covering both core infrastructure and advanced services.
  • Expanded hybrid management scenarios using Azure Arc, Azure Update Manager, and Azure Monitor.
  • Updated security and protocol coverage, including OSConfig baselines, SMB over QUIC, Microsoft Entra Password Protection, and GPU partitioning.

NOTE: We’re not retiring the Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Certification; we’re refreshing the requirements to earn it, with a new single exam that better reflects today's hybrid and cloud-integrated Windows Server administration skills. If you already hold this Certification, no additional action is required on your part. Your Certification will reflect the new name after Exam AZ-802 goes live in September 2026; however, you may take Exam AZ-802. Note that passing the new exam will reset your Certification’s expiration date to one year from the date that you pass that exam rather than a year from your existing Certification’s expiration date. When you renew your certification, you will be assessed on the new skills added to this certification. For more details on the retirement of Exam AZ-800 and Exam AZ-801, read our recent blog post, The AI job boom is here. Are you ready to showcase your skills?

Ready to prove your skills?

Take advantage of the discounted beta exam offer. The first 300 people who take Exam AZ-802 (beta) on or before July 22, 2026, can get 80% off.

item.title: Microsoft Credentials roundup: June 2026
item.description:
Read about Pro Badges, AI-driven Certifications, and Applied Skills, where learning meets today’s work. And find out how training service providers helped 153,000 learners develop AI skills.

This has been a big season for Microsoft Credentials.

With the introduction of Microsoft Pro Badges, a growing portfolio of AI-focused Microsoft Certifications, and expanded Microsoft Applied Skills offerings, we’re continuing to evolve how skills are built, validated, and recognized, closer to practical application.

Here’s what’s new, what’s changing, and what’s ahead.

Introducing Microsoft Pro Badges

Microsoft Pro Badges, the first credentials of their kind, recognize real-world skills and proficiencies demonstrated through everyday work without separate exams. At their core is Verified Proficiency, our proprietary tool that measures and assesses performance through product telemetry, securely capturing evidence of your skills as you work.

The first Pro Badge covers GitHub Copilot Verified Proficiencies. It had a soft launch at Microsoft Build in early June 2026 and will become generally available at GitHub Universe in late October 2026.

Join the GitHub Copilot Verified Proficiency Insiders List to be among the first to get early updates.

New Certifications: Built for an AI-first world

We’ve launched one of our largest Certification expansions in recent years, spanning AI, data, security, development, and business applications.

These new Certifications are designed to:

  • Reflect how roles are evolving in an AI-driven workplace.
  • Help you build capabilities for emerging AI-first jobs.
  • Align closely to today’s job roles, helping you to build skills that you can apply immediately.

Since February 2026, we’ve introduced 17 new Certifications and exams, now either in beta or widely available:

item.title: Microsoft AI Skills Fest wraps—and the momentum continues
item.description:
AI Skills Fest, June 8–12, 2026, brought together a dynamic global community to build practical AI skills. Here’s what to do next and how to keep building on what you’ve learned.

Wow, what a week!

One of my favorite things about Microsoft AI Skills Fest was seeing so many people jump in, try something new, and build practical AI skills together. The festival may be wrapping up, but the energy from this week is still going strong.

Across roles, industries, and experience levels, you explored new tools, sharpened your prompts, and put AI to work in ways that go far beyond a single week.

Want a quick look back? Check out our recap video for standout moments, familiar faces, and even a few bloopers—because no great event is complete without those.

 

 

In just one week, you—and people around the world—really made AI Skills Fest count.

 

 

That’s the power of learning together. And it doesn’t stop here.

item.title: New Microsoft Certified: Dynamics 365 Contact Center AI Engineer Associate Certification
item.description:
Deliver always‑on customer service at scale. Prove your ability to design and run modern contact center solutions in Dynamics 365 that combine agents and human expertise, with Exam AB‑250 (beta).

Customer expectations now demand fast, continuous service across every channel. Meeting that expectation requires contact center solutions that combine human expertise with intelligent automation, while staying scalable, secure, and well governed.

This shift is creating new opportunities for professionals who can translate business and service requirements into modern contact center solutions that work across voice and digital channels.

To support this evolution, we’re introducing the Microsoft Certified: Dynamics 365 Contact Center AI Engineer Associate Certification. It validates your ability to design, implement, and operate contact center as a service (CCaaS) solutions using Dynamics 365 Contact Center and service‑oriented autonomous agents. To earn this new Microsoft Certification, you need to pass Exam AB-250: Transforming Contact Center Experiences with AI in Dynamics 365, currently in beta.

Is this the right Certification for you?

This Certification validates the skills to use AI, Microsoft Copilot, and agents to deliver scalable, always-on service across voice and digital channels.

It assesses a candidate’s ability to:

  • Deploy Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Implement channels
  • Configure agents and AI
  • Configure work distribution
  • Configure the representative experience
  • Manage Contact Center analytics

Candidates collaborate with customer service leaders, contact center managers, IT teams, and legal and compliance stakeholders to ensure solutions align with operational goals, policies, and responsible AI principles, including security, data protection, transparency, and accountability.

They should have experience with Microsoft Power Platform and Microsoft Teams and know how to use automation, integrations, and AI to optimize service workflows. They should also be able to translate business and service requirements into scalable, well-governed contact center solutions where human representatives and autonomous agents work together securely and compliantly.

Candidates for Exam AB-250 should:

  • Have experience implementing or planning CCaaS solutions.
  • Understand how voice, social, and digital channels are orchestrated in a contact center.
  • Know key contact center roles, including representatives, supervisors, and administrators.
  • Have a basic understanding of agents, AI self-service, and AI-assisted experiences.

Ready to prove your skills?

Take advantage of the discounted beta exam offer. The first 300 people who take Exam AB-250 (beta) on or before June 18, 2026, can get 80% off.
